meta.description: Canonical clinical source register. Every clinical recommendation in the app must trace to an entry here. Entries carry verification status; never mark verified without checking the implemented recommendation against the actual source.
meta.reviewer: automated build-time research (requires named-clinician sign-off before clinical use)

verificationLegend.verified-live: Source opened/checked online on dateChecked and the specific recommendations used in the app were confirmed against it.
verificationLegend.verified-summary: Verified via the publisher's official summary/search result of the source on dateChecked; full-text cross-check still required.
verificationLegend.pending-verification: Known source, not yet re-checked for currency. Content using this entry is flagged in-app.

sources.title: Hypertensive Disorders in Pregnancy — Good Clinical Practice Recommendations (GCPR), 3rd Edition
sources.population: Pregnant and postpartum women in India
sources.postpartumApplicability: Includes de novo postpartum hypertension; normalisation expected by 42nd postpartum day (gestational HTN)
sources.evidenceLevel: Good Clinical Practice Recommendations (consensus + evidence review); National Eclampsia Registry data cited
sources.checkedAgainst: PDF served from fogsi.org (2026 upload path) — definitions, HDP-Gestosis score, treatment threshold ≥140/90 (WOG), targets ≤140/90, delivery timing (GH term; mild PE 37 wks; severe PE after 34 wks; eclampsia deliver once stabilised post-MgSO4; ≤24 wks immediate delivery better; individualise 24–33+6)

sources.title: The 2021 ISSHP classification, diagnosis & management recommendations for international practice
sources.postpartumApplicability: Postpartum BP targets DBP ~85; review at 3 and 6 months; annual CV review 5–10 y
sources.checkedAgainst: Full PDF: standardised BP measurement; proteinuria PrCr ≥30 mg/mmol, ACR ≥8 mg/mmol or ≥300 mg/day or dipstick 2+ if confirmatory testing unavailable; no 'mild/severe' PE label in ongoing pregnancy; treat all HDP with antihypertensives; severe HTN ≥160/110 treat within minutes-hours monitored; target DBP 85; MgSO4 for eclampsia + PE with severe HTN/neuro features; aspirin ≥150 mg night from <16 to 36 wks after multivariable screening; calcium <900 mg/d intake → supplement ≥500 mg/d; exercise recommended; LMWH/vitC/E/folate NOT for PE prevention

sources.title: Practice Advisory: Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP trial update to PB 222)
sources.population: Mild chronic hypertension in pregnancy (CHAP trial population)
sources.evidenceLevel: CHAP RCT n=2408: treatment <140/90 reduced preeclampsia with severe features, indicated preterm birth <35w, abruption, fetal/neonatal death; no increase SGA
sources.checkedAgainst: Publisher summary + independent 2025 review confirming advisory remains operative: initiate/titrate therapy at ≥140/90 mmHg for chronic HTN (treatment threshold, not target). Note ACOG PB222 base document last reaffirmed — verify current reaffirmation date when next audited.

sources.topic: Routine antenatal care model, nutrition, maternal/fetal assessment
sources.title: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience (+ updates: MMN supplements, vitamin D, zinc, ultrasound before 24 weeks; WHO Maternal Health recommendations 2nd ed 2025)
sources.checkedAgainst: WHO pages + NCBI compendium: daily IFA 30–60 mg elemental iron + 400 µg folic acid; intermittent IFA only where daily not acceptable & anaemia prevalence <20%; anaemia in ANC → 120 mg elemental iron daily until Hb normal; MMS recommended only within rigorous research contexts (supersedes 2016); ≥8 contacts

sources.title: Consolidated guidelines for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage
sources.version: Consolidated edition (supersedes fragmented prior guidance incl. 2012 PPH recs; incorporates 2017 TXA recs, 2018 uterotonics, 2023 blood-loss assessment/treatment bundle)
sources.population: Women during pregnancy, childbirth & immediate postpartum, any setting
sources.evidenceLevel: GRADE; e.g., Rec 7 uterotonics UPDATED (oxytocin/carbetocin/misoprostol); Rec 14/15 NEW: TXA NOT for prevention (vaginal or caesarean); Rec 27 TXA for TREATMENT retained; Rec 29 TXA within treatment bundle
sources.checkedAgainst: WHO page + NCBI full recommendations chapter + Bleeding-after-birth provider guide: PPH definition >500 mL vaginal / >1000 mL CS or any loss compromising haemodynamics; TXA 1 g IV over 10 min as early as possible within 3 h of birth, repeat 1 g if bleeding continues at 30 min or restarts within 24 h; oxytocin 10 IU in 100–500 mL IV as fast as possible within bundle; TXA-bupivacaine storage separation warning; heat-stable carbetocin context where cold chain unavailable

sources.title: Intrapartum care (NG235)
sources.version: NG235 (replaces CG190); updates Nov 2025 water birth, Jun 2025 fluid balance/bladder care/hyponatraemia, Jun 2026 vitamin K deficiency bleeding prevention reintroduced

sources.topic: STI treatment (gonorrhoea, chlamydia, syphilis, PID, vaginitis, HSV, etc.)
sources.title: Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021
sources.region: USA (globally used; adapt to local resistance patterns)
sources.checkedAgainst: CDC pages + wall chart: uncomplicated gonorrhoea cervix/urethra/rectum → ceftriaxone 500 mg IM single dose (<150 kg; 1 g if ≥150 kg); pharyngeal same; conjunctivitis 1 g IM; DGI 1 g IV/IM q24h; PID outpatient → ceftriaxone 500 mg IM ×1 + doxycycline 100 BD ×14 d + metronidazole 500 BD ×14 d; chlamydia doxycycline 100 BD ×7 d (pregnancy → azithromycin); trichomonas metronidazole 500 mg BD ×7 d (women); bacterial vaginosis metronidazole 500 BD ×7 d etc.; test-of-cure/retest intervals per section; EPT provisions US-specific (not applicable India)

sources.topic: Legal framework for termination of pregnancy (India)
sources.title: Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act 1971 as amended by MTP (Amendment) Act 2021 + MTP (Amendment) Rules 2021 amending Rules 2003
sources.publishedDate: Act assent 2021-03-25, in force 2021-09-24; Rules notified 2021-10-12
sources.version: Current law as of 2026-08-23 (no later amendment found in search)
sources.population: All women seeking termination in India
sources.gestationalAge: ≤20 wks: 1 RMP opinion; >20–24 wks: 2 RMPs for Rule 3B categories (rape/incest survivors, minors, marital-status change, major physical disability (RPwD Act 2016), mental illness, substantial foetal malformation risk, humanitarian/disaster settings); >24 wks: only via State Medical Board (gynaecologist, paediatrician, radiologist/sonologist + others) for substantial foetal abnormality — Board opinion within 3 days, procedure within 5 days; no gestation limit where life of woman at risk; medical-method provider norms (≤9 wks MMA: 3 months OBG experience or 10 supervised cases)
sources.checkedAgainst: Official Gazette text + SCC/LiveLaw notifications; Section 5A confidentiality (disclosure punishable up to 1 yr); place-of-performance restriction s.4; failure-of-device presumption explanation; rape anguish presumption Explanation 2

sources.title: 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
sources.version: 2023 (updates 2018; diagnosis criteria retained: 2 of 3 [hyperandrogenism/OV dysfunction/PCOM] with AMH now acceptable alternative to ultrasound in adults; adolescents need hyperandrogenism + OV dysfunction)
sources.checkedAgainst: Guideline recommendation extracts: letrozole first-line pharmacological ovulation induction (off-label caveat); clomiphene > metformin alone; gonadotrophins second line low-dose step-up; laparoscopic ovarian surgery alternative second line; IVF after failed 1st/2nd line with antagonist protocol + agonist trigger/freezing strategy for OHSS risk reduction; psychological screening; metabolic/CVD/sleep surveillance; inositol experimental

sources.title: WHO recommendation on tranexamic acid for the treatment of postpartum haemorrhage (WOMAN-trial based)
sources.version: Supersedes 2012 TXA recommendation; now folded into Consolidated PPH 2025 Recs 27/29
sources.population: Clinically diagnosed PPH after vaginal birth or CS
sources.postpartumApplicability: Within 3 h of birth (reference point = time of birth)
sources.evidenceLevel: Strong rec, moderate-quality evidence (WOMAN trial n=20,060)
sources.checkedAgainst: IRIS PDF: 1 g in 10 mL (100 mg/mL) IV at 1 mL/min (over 10 min); 2nd dose 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 min or restarts within 24 h; do not initiate beyond 3 h unless treating restarted bleeding within 24 h window; benefit falls ~10% per 15-min delay
